title: $100,000 slashed: Intel possibly ends Bug Bounty payouts
content_md:
$100,000 slashed: Intel possibly ends Bug Bounty payouts

Intel has suspended its existing bug bounty program and launched a new vulnerability disclosure program on Intigriti that explicitly offers no bounties. The previous program paid researchers between $250 and $100,000 depending on severity and product class, with the highest rewards for critical hardware vulnerabilities. Critical firmware bugs paid up to $30,000 and software bugs up to $10,000.

The new program, launched September 17, is described as a responsible disclosure program "without bounties." Intel's own website still promotes the old bounty program with rewards up to $100,000, creating confusion. Intel has not stated a reason for the change. In 2020, 105 of 231 CVEs handled by Intel came through the bug bounty program, which launched in 2017 for select researchers and opened to the public in 2018.

It remains unclear whether this is a permanent elimination of bounties or a program restructuring. In January, Intel had announced plans to evolve its bounty criteria during 2026, including additional bonuses for high-quality reports and exceptional proof-of-concept demonstrations.
